This is commonly used to inject configuration objects that shouldn't come from user-provided data.\n\n## The Security Vulnerability\n\nBy default, `@JacksonInject` allows the injected value to be overridden by values in the JSON input if a matching property key exists. This creates a security vulnerability where attackers can bypass server-side configurations.\n\n### Vulnerable Pattern\n\n```java\n@JsonCreator\npublic MyClass(\n    @JsonProperty(\"data\") String data,\n    @JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig config  // Can be overridden!\n) {\n    this.data = data;\n    this.config = config;\n}\n```\n\nWith the above code, an attacker can send:\n```json\n{\n    \"data\": \"value\",\n    \"\": { \"enabled\": true }\n}\n```\n\nThe empty key `\"\"` matches the unnamed `@JacksonInject` parameter and overrides the server's configuration.\n\n## The Fix: Using useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE\n\nTo prevent JSON input from overriding injected values, use the `useInput` parameter:\n\n```java\nimport com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JacksonInject;\nimport com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.OptBoolean;\n\n@JsonCreator\npublic MyClass(\n    @JsonProperty(\"data\") String data,\n    @JacksonInject(useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE) JavaScriptConfig config  // Safe!\n) {\n    this.data = data;\n    this.config = config;\n}\n```\n\n### OptBoolean Values\n\n- `OptBoolean.TRUE` - Always use input from JSON if available (default behavior for some versions)\n- `OptBoolean.FALSE` - Never use input from JSON; always use injected value\n- `OptBoolean.DEFAULT` - Use default behavior (depends on Jackson version and configuration)\n\n## When to Apply This Fix\n\nApply `useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE` to any `@JacksonInject` annotation where:\n\n1. The injected value is a security-sensitive configuration (e.g., `JavaScriptConfig`)\n2. The injected value controls feature toggles or permissions\n3. The injected value should never be user-controlled\n\n## Jackson Version Notes\n\n- Available since Jackson 2.6+\n- The default behavior may vary between Jackson versions\n- For security-critical applications, always explicitly set `useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE`\n\n## Testing the Fix\n\nAfter applying the fix, verify that:\n\n1. Legitimate requests without the exploit still work\n2. Requests with empty key `\"\"` or any attempt to override the injected value are rejected or use the server config\n3. The actual server-side configuration is always used\n\n## References\n\n- Jackson @JacksonInject documentation\n- CVE-2021-25646 (Apache Druid vulnerability)\n- CVE-2021-26919 (Apache Druid second bypass)\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":13,"cache_creation_input_tokens":361,"cache_read_input_tokens":42917,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":361,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":1},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c057f2fc-15dd-4a2b-9a81-824eef9ea731","uuid":"8005d680-c044-4fb7-9a9f-f3df0e8b3cd5"}

This is useful for distributing fixes without needing to share entire branches.\n\n## Creating Patches\n\n### Method 1: git diff (Uncommitted Changes)\n\nCreate a patch from uncommitted changes:\n```bash\ngit diff > my_changes.patch\n```\n\nFor staged changes only:\n```bash\ngit diff --cached > staged_changes.patch\n```\n\n### Method 2: git format-patch (Committed Changes)\n\nCreate patches from commits:\n```bash\n# Last N commits\ngit format-patch -N\n\n# Specific commit range\ngit format-patch origin/main..HEAD\n\n# Single commit\ngit format-patch -1 <commit-hash>\n```\n\n### Method 3: Manual Patch File (Unified Diff Format)\n\nCreate a patch file manually in unified diff format:\n\n```diff\n--- a/path/to/original/file.java\n+++ b/path/to/modified/file.java\n@@ -line_start,line_count +line_start,line_count @@\n context line (unchanged)\n-removed line\n+added line\n context line (unchanged)\n```\n\n## Patch File Format\n\nA unified diff patch contains:\n\n1. **Header lines**:\n   - `--- a/path/to/file` (original file)\n   - `+++ b/path/to/file` (modified file)\n\n2. **Hunk headers**: `@@ -start,count +start,count @@`\n   - `-start,count` refers to original file\n   - `+start,count` refers to modified file\n\n3. **Content lines**:\n   - Lines starting with ` ` (space) are context (unchanged)\n   - Lines starting with `-` are removed\n   - Lines starting with `+` are added\n\n## Applying Patches\n\n### Using git apply\n\n```bash\n# Apply a patch\ngit apply my_patch.patch\n\n# Check if patch applies cleanly (dry run)\ngit apply --check my_patch.patch\n\n# Apply with verbose output\ngit apply -v my_patch.patch\n\n# Apply patch with some fuzz (context flexibility)\ngit apply --fuzz=3 my_patch.patch\n```\n\n### Using patch command\n\n```bash\n# Apply from repo root\npatch -p1 < my_patch.patch\n\n# Dry run\npatch -p1 --dry-run < my_patch.patch\n\n# Reverse a patch\npatch -R -p1 < my_patch.patch\n```\n\nThe `-p1` strips the leading `a/` or `b/` from paths.\n\n## Best Practices\n\n1. **Include context**: Use at least 3 lines of context around changes\n2. **Test patches**: Always do a dry run before applying\n3. **Atomic patches**: Create separate patches for independent changes\n4. **Clear naming**: Use descriptive patch file names\n5. **Document changes**: Include comments explaining the fix\n\n## Handling Conflicts\n\nIf a patch doesn't apply cleanly:\n\n1. Check if files have been modified since patch creation\n2. Use `--3way` option for three-way merge\n3. Manually edit the patch to update context lines\n4. Use `--ignore-whitespace` for whitespace issues\n\n## Example: Security Patch\n\n```diff\n--- a/src/main/java/com/example/MyClass.java\n+++ b/src/main/java/com/example/MyClass.java\n@@ -22,6 +22,7 @@\n\n import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JacksonInject;\n import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonCreator;\n+import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.OptBoolean;\n import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonProperty;\n\n public class MyClass {\n@@ -35,7 +36,7 @@ public class MyClass {\n     @JsonCreator\n     public MyClass(\n         @JsonProperty(\"data\") String data,\n-        @JacksonInject Config config\n+        @JacksonInject(useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE) Config config\n     ) {\n         this.data = data;\n         this.config = config;\n```\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":13,"cache_creation_input_tokens":361,"cache_read_input_tokens":42917,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":361,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":1},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c057f2fc-15dd-4a2b-9a81-824eef9ea731","uuid":"bbb89d9c-89e4-4f51-abbd-94c49badc11b"}
